To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we successfully synthesized a new molybdenum sulfide with a high content of sulfur, Mo15S18, and that we demonstrated the potential of this material as a lubricant for steel–steel sliding contact.
the synthesis of Mo15S19 nanoparticulated lubricating oil is a promising strategy for reducing wear and friction in steel–steel contacts.
Mo15S19 nanocrystalline particles were successfully synthesized in a linseed oil matrix and their tribological properties were evaluated in steel–steel contacts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a new type of molybdenum sulfide nanoparticles with interesting tribological properties, which could be used in future lubricant formulations.
the synthesis of Mo15S19 nanocrystals and their use as lubricant additives.
the synthesis of Mo15S19 as a lubricant for steel–steel sliding contact and its lubricating performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nanoparticles of Mo15S19 synthesized in this study are a potential candidate to be used as an additive in lubricants.

the lubricant additive Mo15S19 has been successfully prepared and its tribological behavior has been studied, showing that the nanoparticles can be used as a lubricant additive for steel–steel sliding contact.
the Mo15S19 nanoparticle–linseed oil mixture is an excellent lubricant that reduces friction and wear, which is a consequence of the formation of a tribofilm on the steel surface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Mo15S19 is a promising additive in lubricating oil formulations.

the Mo15S19 nanoparticulated lubricant has shown a good tribological performance, which could be improved by optimizing its dispersion and by increasing the concentration of the nanoparticles in the base oil.
the use of Mo15S19 as a lubricant in steel–steel sliding contact is promising, but further studies are needed to optimize the tribological behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lubricating properties of Mo15S19 are not only due to the nanoparticles but also to the formation of the molybdenum oxide layer, which is a key factor in the tribological behavior of this system.
Mo15S19 can be used as a lubricant in the absence of any additional additives.
nanoparticles of Mo15S19 can be synthesized in linseed oil, avoiding the use of toxic organic solvents, with a high degree (95%) of yield.
